title: Three metrics, one pair of points

prereqs.why: The three metrics being compared are the Euclidean, taxicab and maximum metrics.

statement:
On $\R^2$, write $x = (0, 0)$ and $y = (3, 4)$, and take the three standard metrics

$$d_2(x,y) = \sqrt{(x_1-y_1)^2 + (x_2-y_2)^2}$$

$$d_1(x,y) = |x_1-y_1| + |x_2-y_2|$$

$$d_\infty(x,y) = \max\bigl(|x_1-y_1|,\, |x_2-y_2|\bigr)$$

Give the value of

$$d_1(x,y) - d_2(x,y) + d_\infty(x,y).$$
hints: Compute the three separately before combining them. The coordinate differences are $3$ and $4$ in every case; only what you do with them changes.
$d_2$ is the hypotenuse of a 3–4–5 triangle, so it comes out whole. $d_1$ adds, and $d_\infty$ takes the larger.

payload.label: Your answer
payload.syntax: A number. You can write arithmetic and roots: 7 - sqrt(25) + 4.
